newsitem.title: USA: Doe Run lead output hit by roof collapse - trade.
newsitem.headline: Doe Run lead output hit by roof collapse - trade.

text.p: Lead output by U.S. producer Doe Run has been cut because of last week's roof collapse at a reverberatory furnace at the company's Buick recycling facility in Missouri, traders and analysts said.
Officials at the company's head office in St Louis were not immediately available for comment.
Market observers and traders understood Buick was operating at about 80,000 tons of lead per year, and that repairs would take 45 to 60 days.
"This could take about 10,000 tons out of the market over the next two months," an observer said.
"It should tighten things up considerably and should result in imports from Canada and Mexico, which could put a squeeze on metal elsewhere and possibly result in a drawdown of LME stocks," he added.
Lead stocks in the U.S. fell to 7,777 short tons at the end of October from 13,497 short tons at the end of September, the American Bureau of Metal Statistics reported last week.
Lead premiums are still in the 3.00 to 4.00 cents range, though some upward pressure may be felt following the incident at Doe Run, traders said.
Doe Run also produces primary lead at the company's much bigger Herculaneum plant, also in Missouri.
